subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group isolation stay within configurable sender/topic session routing and explicit thread-bound subagents, or should OpenClaw add automatic per-sender group subagent lifecycle with per-user skills, config, memory, admin controls, and cleanup?
rationale: The requested behavior spans Feishu channel routing, session state, per-agent config and skill authorization, memory isolation, quota/cost control, and lifecycle cleanup, which requires product and security intent before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Seams
options.body: Document and improve groupSessionScope, bindings, and explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported Feishu group pattern, splitting any remaining gaps into smaller issues.

options.title: Design Plugin-Owned Automation
options.body: Approve a Feishu plugin-owned automatic per-sender subagent design with explicit storage, security, config-write, quota, and cleanup contracts before any implementation PR.

options.title: Split Into Canonical Pieces
options.body: Break this request into sender memory isolation, user skill preferences, threading-policy ergonomics, and lifecycle/admin-control issues owned by the relevant surfaces.

recommendation.title: Narrow To Existing Seams
recommendation.body: Document and improve groupSessionScope, bindings, and explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported Feishu group pattern, splitting any remaining gaps into smaller issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin is documented as community maintained by @m1heng, and this is primarily a Feishu product and ownership decision.
